enriched_description: Social hymenopteran insect measuring 2-25 mm with distinctly segmented body comprising head, mesosoma, and metasoma connected by narrow petiole (waist). Integument typically black, brown, or red with glossy or matte finish. Head with elbowed antennae bearing 10-12 segments and prominent mandibles. Mesosoma robust with three pairs of legs adapted for walking and climbing. Metasoma bulbous containing defensive glands. Winged reproductive forms (alates) possess two pairs of membranous wings during breeding season; workers wingless. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body plan, and six jointed legs. Colony exhibits caste polymorphism.

Orthopteran insect measuring 15-75 mm with elongated cylindrical body. Integument green, brown, or gray providing cryptic coloration. Head hypognathous with short filiform antennae and large compound eyes. Hind legs (metathoracic) massively enlarged with muscular femora adapted for powerful saltatorial locomotion. Forewings (tegmina) leathery and narrow; hind wings broad membranous and folded fan-like at rest. Tympanal organs on first abdominal segment. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body with three tagmata, and six jointed legs. Terrestrial plant-eater with chewing mouthparts.

Orthopteran insect measuring 10-50 mm with somewhat flattened body. Integument black, brown, or reddish-brown. Head with long filiform antennae exceeding body length. Hind legs enlarged for leaping. Forewings (tegmina) modified into stridulatory organs; males produce chirping sounds by rubbing specialized file and scraper structures on forewings together. Hind wings membranous and folded beneath tegmina. Cerci elongated and filamentous. Ovipositor in females needle-like. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body plan, and six jointed legs. Nocturnal with tympanal hearing organs on fore tibiae.

Phasmid insect with extremely elongated cylindrical body measuring 50-300 mm resembling twigs or branches. Integument brown, green, or gray with textured surface mimicking bark. Body proportions extremely slender with length-to-width ratio exceeding 10:1. Legs long and thin with expanded femora in some species bearing leaf-like lobes. Antennae filiform and elongate. Wings reduced or absent in most species. Exhibits remarkable cryptic coloration and posture-based camouflage. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body with three tagmata, and six jointed legs. Primarily tropical with nocturnal feeding habits.

Dictyopteran insect measuring 10-80 mm with dorsoventrally flattened oval body. Integument glossy in shades of brown, black, or reddish-brown. Head concealed beneath pronotum (shield-like thoracic segment). Antennae long and filiform with numerous segments. Legs spiny and cursorial adapted for rapid running. Forewings (tegmina) leathery; hind wings membranous and folded beneath. Cerci short and segmented. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body plan, and six jointed legs. Nocturnal with omnivorous feeding habits. Ootheca egg cases produced by females.

Dictyopteran insect measuring 30-150 mm with elongated body and highly modified raptorial forelegs. Head triangular and highly mobile with large compound eyes and three ocelli. Antennae filiform and slender. Forelegs (raptorial) with spined femur and tibia forming grasping mechanism; held folded in characteristic prayer-like posture. Mesothorax elongated providing reach for striking. Wings well-developed; forewings leathery, hind wings broad and membranous. Abdomen slender and flexible. Integument green, brown, or mottled for camouflage. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body, and six jointed legs. Predacious with stereoscopic vision.

Homopteran insect measuring 20-50 mm with stout broad body. Head wide with prominent compound eyes set wide apart and three ocelli. Antennae short and bristle-like. Two pairs of membranous wings with distinctive venation; wings held roof-like over abdomen at rest. Male abdomen contains paired tymbal organs (drum-like membranes) producing high-pitched resonant calls. Body coloration brown, green, or black with translucent wings showing prominent veins. Legs short with robust femora. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body with three tagmata, and six jointed legs. Nymphs subterranean for extended periods.

Small homopteran insect measuring 3-12 mm with wedge-shaped body tapering posteriorly. Integument green, yellow, brown, or patterned with distinctive markings. Head broad with row of ocellar setae between compound eyes. Antennae short and bristle-like arising between eyes. Wings membranous and held tent-like over body; forewings with distinctive venation. Hind legs adapted for jumping with rows of spines on tibiae. Body laterally compressed. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body plan, and six jointed legs. Small leaping insect that feeds by sucking plant juices using piercing-sucking mouthparts.

Neuropteran insect measuring 10-25 mm with delicate elongated body. Two pairs of large membranous wings with extensive network of fine veins creating lace-like appearance. Wings held roof-like over body at rest. Body soft and slender in green, brown, or yellow. Antennae long and filiform often exceeding body length. Head with prominent compound eyes; mouthparts adapted for predation. Legs slender and delicate. Abdomen elongate and flexible. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body with three tagmata, and six jointed legs. Larvae are aphid-lions with sickle-shaped mandibles.

Odonate insect measuring 30-120 mm with slender elongated body. Two pairs of large membranous wings with intricate venation; wings held horizontally at rest. Head dominated by enormous compound eyes covering most of head surface with three small ocelli. Antennae short and bristle-like. Thorax robust and oblique. Abdomen extremely elongate and slender comprising 10 segments. Integument iridescent in blue, green, red, or yellow with metallic sheen. Legs spiny and adapted for grasping prey in flight. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body plan, and six jointed legs. Adults and nymphs are voracious predators of mosquitoes.
